headline: Chris and Jordy deadlocked at the top after four go 2-0
dek: A rare week where a full third of the pool went undefeated, but Chris and Jordy maintain their co-lead on net points. Meanwhile, Adrian and Taras both got blanked to fall further behind.
takeaways: Four 2-0 weeks in one round — Ben, Chris, Jordy, and Tymko all kept both teams rolling while the other five went a combined 3-7.
Chris's Bills and Pack outscored their opponents by a combined 35 points, enough to hold off Jordy's Lions and Broncos (up 15) for the tiebreaker at the top.
Ben's Texans hung 44 on Taras's winless Chargers in the most lopsided result of the week, while C.J. Stroud threw five touchdowns in LA.
Adrian's brutal 0-2 drops him into a tie with Matej at 8 points, and both teams got torched — the Patriots gave up 45 to the Pack, the Bucs couldn't hold a late lead in Chicago.

games.text:
Matej's Jags rolled into Baltimore and absolutely dismantled Orest's Ravens 33-10 in a head-to-head that was never in doubt. Trevor Lawrence went 16-for-26 for 242 yards and a touchdown, while the Ravens offense sputtered badly — backup quarterback J. Fagnano threw two picks on just 18 attempts and managed only 60 yards through the air. Justice Hill provided the lone bright spot for Baltimore with 85 rushing yards and a touchdown on nine carries, but it wasn't nearly enough.

The win pushes Matej to 8 points and keeps his Jags rolling at 6-2, even as his Eagles continue to languish. Orest splits the week at 1-1, his Ravens falling to 4-5 and now staring down a Monday night date with Taras's 0-8 Chargers — a game he desperately needs after this drubbing.

Bill's Cowboys survived a road scare in Indianapolis, holding off the Colts 27-23 behind a monster day from Dak Prescott (335 yards, 2 TDs) and CeeDee Lamb, who torched the Indy secondary for 10 catches and 195 yards. Jamaal Williams punched in a rushing touchdown to go with his 101 yards on the ground, giving Dallas just enough cushion. The Colts made it interesting late — Adonai Dulin hauled in a 55-yard touchdown from Daniel Jones — but couldn't complete the comeback.

Bill picks up the win in his only game of the week, moving to 10 points and keeping pace in the middle of the pack. His Boys improve to 4-5 and face a massive Sunday late-afternoon test in Week 10: Ben's 7-1 Niners come to town. His Steelers also get Cincinnati on Sunday night.

Tymko's Chiefs handled their business at Arrowhead, crushing the visiting Jets 35-12 in a game that was effectively over by halftime. Patrick Mahomes was efficient (23-for-31, 242 yards, 2 TDs), and Kenneth Walker III gashed New York on the ground for 102 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries. The Jets managed just four field goals against a suffocating Kansas City defense, and Geno Smith's 165 passing yards offered little resistance.

The Chiefs improve to 6-2 and Tymko sits third in the pool at 11 points after sweeping the week. He gets a softer Sunday slate in Week 10 — KC travels to Atlanta while his Rams head to Arizona — both winnable games to keep him within striking distance of the leaders.

Jordy's Lions won ugly in Miami, grinding out a 19-9 road victory behind Jahmyr Gibbs's 74 rushing yards and a touchdown. Jared Goff wasn't spectacular (17-for-25, 170 yards), but he didn't need to be — the Lions defense stifled Malik Willis and the Dolphins offense all afternoon, holding Miami to just nine points and forcing a Willis interception. Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in eight catches for 86 yards to keep the chains moving.

Detroit improves to 6-2 and Jordy remains tied atop the pool standings with Chris at 13 points, though he trails on net points by 49. Next week brings a critical Sunday morning head-to-head in London: Adrian's Patriots visit the Lions. Jordy also had his Broncos win at Carolina, completing a clean 2-0 week.

Matej's Eagles continued their miserable season, falling at home to the Giants 19-11 in a game that featured more punts than points. J.J. McCarthy managed the game for New York (12-for-19, 127 yards), leaning on Devin Singletary's 21 carries — even if they netted just 31 yards — and a stout defensive effort. Philly's Joe Milton ran for 64 yards on nine attempts and threw for 169, but couldn't find the end zone and the Eagles offense sputtered.

The loss drops Matej's Eagles to 2-7, easily the worst NFC team in the pool, though his Jags picked up a head-to-head win over Orest's Ravens to salvage a 1-1 week. Philadelphia faces another uphill battle as the season wears on, while the Giants grabbed a rare win.

Tymko's Rams escaped Washington with a 20-13 road win, thanks to Puka Nacua going absolutely nuclear — 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Stafford had to work for it (26-for-43, 228 yards, a TD and a pick), but Blake Corum punched in a rushing score and the Rams defense did enough to hold off Jayden Daniels, who threw for 274 yards and a touchdown but couldn't find another gear late. Van Jefferson's TD catch for Washington kept it close, but the Commanders couldn't close.

The Rams improve to 5-4 and Tymko completes the 2-0 week, his second team alongside the Chiefs to pick up wins. He sits at 11 points, two back of the co-leaders, with both his squads traveling West in Week 10 — the Rams to Arizona, KC to Atlanta.

Jordy's Broncos held off Taras's Panthers 26-21 in a head-to-head shootout in Carolina, where Bo Nix outdueled Bryce Young in a back-and-forth affair. Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns, while Jaleel Coleman punched in a rushing score to provide Denver just enough cushion. Young actually had a strong day (28-for-39, 276 yards, 3 TDs), connecting with Darren Waller for 90 yards and a score, but the Panthers couldn't get a critical stop late and Chuba Hubbard's 79 rushing yards weren't enough.

The win pushes Jordy's Broncos to 7-2 and caps his 2-0 sweep, keeping him tied with Chris at the top of the pool at 13 points. Taras falls to 0-2 on the week and sits dead last at 3 points, his Panthers now 3-5 and his Chargers still searching for their first win at 0-8.

Ben's Texans absolutely obliterated Taras's Chargers 44-22 in Los Angeles in the most lopsided result of Week 9, as C.J. Stroud put on an absolute clinic. Stroud went 21-for-35 for 384 yards and five — count 'em, five — touchdown passes, with Kayshon Boutte hauling in two of them for 125 yards. Justin Herbert did his best to keep the Chargers competitive (193 yards, a TD), but three turnovers and a porous defense doomed LA to their eighth straight loss to open the season.

Ben sweeps the week 2-0, his Texans improving to 3-5 while his Niners cruised past the Raiders. He moves to 10 points, fourth in the pool, and gets both teams in action Week 10 — Houston travels to Cleveland, and Sunday late afternoon brings a showdown with Bill's Cowboys when the 7-1 Niners visit Dallas.

Chris's Packers throttled Adrian's Patriots 45-27 in Foxborough in a head-to-head that saw Jordan Love carve up New England's secondary for 372 yards and three touchdowns on 23-of-29 passing. Christian Watson torched the Pats for 171 yards and a score on seven catches, while Keaton Johnson added 68 rushing yards and a TD on the ground. Drake Maye tried to keep the Patriots in it with 299 yards and three touchdowns, but his three interceptions and a shaky defense turned this one into a blowout.

Chris completes the 2-0 week and remains tied with Jordy atop the standings at 13 points, holding the tiebreaker on net points (+94 to +45). Adrian gets blanked 0-2 on the week, his Patriots falling to 5-4 and his Bucs losing a heartbreaker in Chicago. He's now tied with Matej at 8 points, seventh place, and faces Jordy's 6-2 Lions in London next Sunday morning.

Ben's Niners had little trouble dispatching the Raiders 38-17 at Levi's Stadium, as Brock Purdy threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns and the defense forced three Kirk Cousins interceptions. Jalen Watkins hauled in a TD among his four catches for 86 yards, and Kyren Black added 70 rushing yards to keep the Raiders defense off balance. Brock Bowers did his best for Las Vegas with 111 receiving yards, but three Cousins picks made this one a laugher by the fourth quarter.

The win pushes Ben's Niners to 7-1, the best NFC record in the pool, and gives him a 2-0 week. San Francisco heads to Dallas in Week 10 for a Sunday late-afternoon clash with Bill's Cowboys — a huge head-to-head looms between two pool contenders.

Orest's Seahawks shut down the Cardinals 17-3 at home, as Drew Lock managed the game efficiently (19-for-28, 175 yards, a TD) and Zach Charbonnet pounded away for 77 rushing yards on 16 carries. Arizona's offense was completely stifled — Gardner Minshew threw for just 166 yards and the Cardinals never found the end zone, settling for a single field goal. It was an ugly win, but a win nonetheless.

The victory salvages a 1-1 week for Orest after his Ravens got demolished by Matej's Jags in the early window. His Seahawks improve to 5-4, and he gets both teams in action Week 10 — Seattle travels to Las Vegas on Sunday, and Monday night brings another head-to-head when Taras's 0-8 Chargers visit Baltimore.

Adrian's Bucs blew a late lead in Chicago, falling 27-24 to the Bears in a game that featured eight combined turnovers. Baker Mayfield threw two picks and couldn't move the ball when it mattered, while Bucky Irving's 97 rushing yards and two touchdowns kept Tampa in it. Caleb Williams was far from sharp for Chicago (four interceptions), but Luther Burden III hauled in seven catches for 97 yards and a score, and the Bears defense came up with the stops they needed late.

The loss completes a miserable 0-2 week for Adrian, who also saw his Patriots get crushed by Chris's Packers. He falls to 8 points, tied with Matej for seventh, and his Bucs drop to 3-6. Week 10 offers little relief — his Patriots face Jordy's Lions in London on Sunday morning.

Chris's Bills dominated Minnesota 23-6 in a game that was never competitive, as Josh Allen threw for 234 yards and a touchdown and James Cook rumbled for 107 yards and a score on 31 carries. The Vikings offense was completely inept — Carson Wentz managed just 81 yards on 8-of-25 passing and threw two interceptions, and Minnesota never found any rhythm. Justin Jefferson's 58 receiving yards were the lone bright spot in an otherwise dismal afternoon for the Vikes.

The win pushes Chris's Bills to 7-1 and completes his 2-0 sweep alongside the Packers' blowout of Adrian's Patriots. He remains tied with Jordy at 13 points atop the pool, holding the edge on net points. Both his teams play Sunday — the Bills travel to the Jets, the Pack host Minnesota at Lambeau.
